finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches an attacker-supplied URL. Its only check is a suffix match on the parsed hostname, so hosts such as attackerexample.com or evilexample.com pass. The server can be made to request attacker-chosen hosts, and via DNS rebinding internal addresses or cloud metadata. Response disclosure is limited to length and status, so severity is HIGH.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 — `url: str` query parameter on unauthenticated GET /mirror
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 — `await c.get(url)` using httpx.AsyncClient with the full original URL

trace.note: url query param becomes attacker-controlled input
host.endswith("example.com") is a suffix check, not strict set membership; does not close SSRF per ssrf/SKILL.md
c.get(url) dispatches the request to the unvalidated original URL

finding.guards_checked: Suffix-only hostname check (mirror.py:13) judged insufficient; ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) defined but unused; httpx.AsyncClient does not follow redirects by default so no redirect bypass (version unverified); no DNS/IP-range validation; no internal-only binding, so public ingress; no authentication on the route; /ping (mirror.py:23) uses a hardcoded URL and is not a finding.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the suffix match `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, which is one of the insufficient patterns. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is defined but never used. No auth dependency on the route (mirror.py:10-11), and no IP-range or DNS validation. The httpx client at mirror.py:15-16 uses default settings, so redirects are not followed, which is not a bypass.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) unchanged, and the only gate is the suffix check at mirror.py:13, so hosts like attackerexample.com pass; the route is unauthenticated, so this is CONFIRMED. Severity is outside what I verified: the response discloses only length (mirror.py:17), which the candidate already notes.
